title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned government-cloud release from the documented administrator-created auto-labeling policy. The controls, licensing statements and January CY2027 target are supported; the unanswered questions are appropriately limited to existing-file behaviour and government-cloud rollout.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn documents an administrator-created auto-labeling policy to apply library defaults to eligible existing files.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.claim: The documented existing-file policy is admin-opt-in: an administrator creates and turns on the policy before it applies labels.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy ... Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft tells administrators to review simulation results before turning on the existing-file policy.
claims.quote: Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy to confirm that the expected SharePoint sites, document libraries, default library labels, and files are included.

claims.claim: The separate library-default setting page still lists existing files at rest as a limitation.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The library-default setting applies its label to new uploaded files that have no sensitivity label.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied if they don't already have a sensitivity label

claims.claim: The library-default setting applies its label to existing files that are edited when they have no sensitivity label.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied if they don't already have a sensitivity label

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: For the documented new-and-edited-file library setting, a library default overrides a lower-priority label unless it was applied manually.
claims.quote: Default sensitivity label for a document library: Location-based labeling, applicable only for SharePoint. Overrides a lower-priority label unless manually applied.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling does not apply visual markings to documents.
claims.quote: If the labels you select are configured to use visual markings (headers, footers, watermarks), these markings aren't applied to documents when you use auto-labeling.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A sensitivity label that applies encryption can restrict who opens a file.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted

claims.claim: A label with Let users assign permissions and the Word, PowerPoint and Excel prompt-users checkbox selected is unsuitable for a library default.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected.

claims.claim: A label with User access to content expires set to something other than Never cannot be a library default.
claims.quote: User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.claim: A label with Double Key Encryption selected cannot be a library default.
claims.quote: Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Site admin permissions are required to apply and change a library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Site admin permissions are needed to apply and change the sensitivity label in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Libraries with SharePoint Information Rights Management enabled cannot have a default sensitivity label and therefore lack the default this policy requires.
claims.quote: If a library is enabled for IRM, you won't be able to select a default sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Applied sensitivity label file is the documented audit event for application of library-default sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: use the audit log search tool and the Applied sensitivity label file auditing event from the Sensitivity label activities group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[2].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: ActionScourceDetails 6 identifies application by the documented library-default feature.
claims.quote: identify the value for ActionScourceDetails. A value of 6 is used for when the label was applied because of the default sensitivity label for the document library.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether the existing-file policy uses the same ActionScourceDetails value.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint default library labels existing files auto labeling ActionScourceDetails 6 GCC licensing meter; "existing files" "library" "ActionScourceDetails". Read apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-default-label; no policy-specific value stated.

claims.claim: The tooltip for a label applied by the library-default feature reads This file has been automatically labeled.
claims.quote: the tooltip for the label name displays This file has been automatically labeled.

claims.claim: The same tooltip also appears for labels applied by auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies

claims.claim: The same tooltip also appears for a user's default label from a sensitivity label policy, so the column alone does not establish the source.
claims.quote: this tooltip isn't exclusive to the default sensitivity label for a document library. It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies or as a result of a user's default label from sensitivity label policies.

claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services

claims.claim: The licensing requirements for sensitivity-label users depend on the features used.

claims.claim: E3 or Business Premium manual-labeling entitlement does not include automatic labeling.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Manual labeling entitlement doesn't include automatic labeling. Check the feature matrix for an eligible subscription or add-on for the labeling method you intend to use.

claims.claim: The library-default feature requires an eligible premium subscription and applicable prerequisite licences from its service-description entry.
claims.quote: An eligible premium subscription for library default labeling. Check the Apply default sensitivity labeling for SharePoint Document library entry in the Microsoft Purview sensitivity labeling licensing requirements, including the applicable prerequisite licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A licence specific to applying library defaults to existing files, distinct from the published service-side and library-default entitlements, is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview apply default SharePoint library labels existing files licensing pay as you go meter. Read auto-labeling, library-default, get-started and Purview service-description licensing sections; they state general feature entitlements, not a separate existing-file licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A meter specific to applying library defaults to existing files is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview apply default SharePoint library labels existing files licensing pay as you go meter. Read auto-labeling, library-default, get-started and Purview service-description sections; no meter for this policy. The get-started billing statement concerns non-Microsoft 365 Data Map sources.

claims.claim: A label used as a library default must include the scope Files & other data assets.
claims.quote: You've created and published sensitivity labels that include the label scope of Files & other data assets

claims.claim: Labels used as library defaults must be published to the users who select them.
claims.quote: these labels are published to the users who will select a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: You've enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: PDF support must be added in SharePoint if PDFs are to receive sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: To support sensitivity labels for PDFs, you've added support for PDFs in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Creating the existing-file policy requires permission to create and manage auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: You have permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Creating the existing-file policy also requires permission to read the site and library metadata identifying default labels.
claims.quote: You have permission to read the SharePoint site and document library metadata required to identify libraries with default sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The SharePoint library control is reached through document library > Settings > Library settings > Default sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: In SharePoint, navigate to the document library > Settings > Library settings. From the Library settings flyout pane, select Default sensitivity labels, and then select a label from the drop-down box.

claims.claim: POST https://<site-url>/_api/web/lists(guid'<library-guid>') updates the library when used with X-HTTP-Method: MERGE.
claims.quote: The following example shows how to update a list by using the MERGE method. POST https://{site_url}/_api/web/lists(guid'{list_guid}') ... X-HTTP-Method: "MERGE"

claims.claim: DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary is the library setting used by REST automation to set its default label.
claims.quote: For the default library label, set the DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary parameter by using REST API on a library.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to select Extend protection on download, copy, or move when configuring a library default because it supports a different scenario.
claims.quote: From the Library settings pane, select a sensitivity label and don't select the checkbox Extend protection on download, copy, or move. This setting is currently in preview and supports a different labeling scenario.

claims.claim: No administrator UI is documented for the tenant-level switch disabling document-library default labelling.
claims.quote: Searched: "DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling" "admin center"; DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling tenant admin UI existing files auto labeling. Read library-default turn-off instructions and Set-SPOTenant parameter excerpt; the tenant setting requires PowerShell and no UI route was returned.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true turns off the documented tenant-level library-default feature.
claims.quote: This is a tenant-level setting that requires you to use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling parameter set to True ... Set-SpoTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true

claims.claim: The tenant-level library-default switch takes about 15 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: As with all tenant-level configuration changes for SharePoint, it takes about 15 minutes for the change to take effect.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling stops the auto-labeling policy for existing files.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling tenant admin UI existing files auto labeling. Read library-default turn-off instructions and the existing-file policy section of apply-sensitivity-label-automatically; neither states that the switch disables this separate policy type.

claims.claim: After the tenant switch is set, a previously configured library's label selection remains but is deactivated.
claims.quote: The label selection for the document library remains but is deactivated so new files won't have the selected sensitivity label applied.

claims.claim: Turning off the library-default feature does not remove sensitivity labels previously applied as defaults.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that were applied as a default label aren't removed.

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal reaches the audit search control.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -RecordType <ID> is a read-only audit search command.
claims.quote: runs Search-UnifiedAuditLog to search for audit log entries within a specified date range and record type. ... Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate 2023/03/12 -EndDate 2023/03/20 -RecordType <ID>

claims.claim: Updated list is the documented audit event for changes to the library-default label setting.
claims.quote: To audit the configuration setting for this feature, use the Updated list auditing event from the SharePoint list activities group.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The SharePoint Sensitivity column displays the names of labels applied to files.
claims.quote: Use the SharePoint Sensitivity column to see the names of sensitivity labels applied to files.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the feature as helping organisations close labelling gaps for data at rest.
claims.quote: This helps organizations close labeling gaps for data at rest and ensure consistent, secure-by-default protection across SharePoint libraries
